balanced diet = a way of eating that includes a healthy mix of different foods
junk food = unhealthy food that is high in fat, sugar or salt
fizzy drink = a sweet drink with bubbles of gas in it
sparkling water = water with bubbles of gas in it
still water = water without bubbles of gas
dairy = food made from milk, such as cheese or yoghurt
poultry = birds kept for meat or eggs, such as chicken or turkey
seafood = animals from the sea that people eat, such as fish and prawns
wholemeal = made from the whole grain, not just the white part
vegetarian = a person who does not eat meat; food with no meat
ingredients = the foods you need to cook a particular dish
recipe = a set of instructions for cooking a dish
starter = a small dish eaten at the beginning of a meal
main course = the largest part of a meal, usually with meat or a hot dish
dessert = sweet food eaten at the end of a meal
takeaway = a meal you buy and take home to eat
leftovers = food remaining after a meal, often eaten later
book a table = to reserve a place in a restaurant in advance
the bill = the piece of paper that shows how much you must pay
tip = extra money you leave for the waiter
boiled = cooked in hot water
fried = cooked in hot oil
grilled = cooked over or under strong heat
roast = cooked in an oven with fat, often for Sunday lunch
raw = not cooked
spicy = with a hot, strong flavour from spices
bitter = having a sharp taste, like strong coffee or dark chocolate
sour = having an acid taste, like lemon or vinegar
delicious = very pleasant to eat or drink
homemade = made at home, not bought in a shop
allergy = a medical problem caused by eating or touching something
cut down on = to eat or drink less of something
starving = extremely hungry
snack = a small amount of food between meals
breakfast = the first meal of the day
lunch = a meal in the middle of the day
dinner = the main meal in the evening
supper = a light evening meal
brunch = a late morning meal that replaces breakfast and lunch
hungry = wanting or needing food
thirsty = wanting or needing a drink
appetite = the feeling that you want to eat
portion = the amount of food for one person
buffet = a meal where you serve yourself from many dishes
menu = a list of food you can order in a restaurant
oven = a kitchen box that cooks food with hot air
fridge = a cold cupboard that keeps food fresh
freezer = a very cold box for storing frozen food
microwave = a machine that heats food very quickly
saucepan = a deep pan with a handle for cooking on a hob
frying pan = a flat pan for frying food in a little oil
chopping board = a flat board you cut food on
napkin = a piece of cloth or paper for wiping your mouth
kettle = a container for boiling water
toast = bread cooked until it is brown and crisp
cereal = a breakfast food made from grain, often with milk
porridge = a hot breakfast of oats cooked in milk or water
omelette = eggs mixed and cooked flat in a pan
scrambled eggs = eggs stirred while they cook until they are soft
bacon = salted or smoked meat from a pig, often fried
sausage = minced meat in a long skin, often fried
steak = a thick slice of beef, usually grilled
beef = meat from a cow
pork = meat from a pig
lamb = meat from a young sheep
salmon = a pink fish, often grilled or smoked
tuna = a large sea fish, often sold in tins
prawns = small shellfish that are pink when cooked
vegan = eating no animal products, including milk and eggs
gluten-free = made without gluten, for people who cannot eat wheat
organic = grown or made without chemical pesticides or fertilisers
frozen food = food kept at a very low temperature to last longer
tinned food = food stored in a metal can
stale = no longer fresh, especially bread
ripe = ready to eat, of fruit
rotten = too old to eat; going bad
peel = to take the skin off fruit or vegetables
slice = to cut into thin pieces; one such piece
chop = to cut food into small pieces with a knife
stir = to move a spoon around in a liquid or mixture
bake = to cook in an oven, especially bread or cakes
steam = to cook food in the vapour from boiling water
barbecue = cooking food outdoors over a fire; that meal
picnic = a meal eaten outdoors, often in a park
café = a small place that serves drinks and light meals
fast food = food that is prepared and served very quickly
greasy = with a lot of oil or fat on it
salty = tasting of salt
sweet = tasting of sugar; a small sugary food
bland = with little flavour
tasty = having a pleasant flavour
flavour = the taste of a food or drink
herb = a plant used to add taste, such as basil or parsley
spice = a dried seed or powder that makes food hotter or stronger
garlic = a strong-smelling white bulb used in cooking
vinegar = a sour liquid used in salads and pickles
mustard = a hot yellow or brown sauce eaten with meat
ketchup = a sweet tomato sauce
mayonnaise = a thick, creamy cold sauce made with eggs and oil
jam = sweet fruit cooked with sugar, spread on bread
honey = a sweet, thick food made by bees
yoghurt = a thick, slightly sour milk product
pastry = a mixture of flour, fat and water used for pies
biscuit = a small, dry, sweet baked snack
crisps = thin slices of fried potato sold in a bag
lettuce = a green leafy vegetable eaten in salads
cucumber = a long green vegetable with a watery inside
carrot = an orange root vegetable
mushroom = a fungus you can cook, often white or brown
beans = seeds you cook, often from a tin, such as baked beans
lentils = small dried seeds cooked in soups and stews
rice = small white or brown grains cooked in water
pasta = Italian food made from flour and water, in many shapes
flour = a white or brown powder from grain, used for bread and cakes
yeast = a living substance that makes bread rise
dough = a mixture of flour and water before it is baked
sandwich = two pieces of bread with food between them
burger = a round piece of fried meat in a bun
chips = pieces of potato fried in oil
mashed potatoes = potatoes boiled and crushed with butter or milk
gravy = a brown sauce made from meat juices
stew = meat and vegetables cooked slowly in liquid
salad dressing = a sauce of oil and vinegar (or similar) for salad
smoothie = a thick cold drink of blended fruit
lemonade = a sweet drink made with lemon
herbal tea = a hot drink made from herbs, not black tea
sip = to drink a very small amount at a time
chew = to bite food many times before you swallow
swallow = to make food or drink go down your throat
bite = to cut food with your teeth; a small piece you eat
side dish = a small extra dish served with the main course
